cohort: 143 parturients with uterine rupture (29 with delayed diagnosis) identified from 174,189 deliveries at a single large academic tertiary care center between 2005 and 2018
finding: Parturients with delayed diagnosis of uterine rupture had unique characteristics (unscarred uterus, epidural analgesia, grand-multiparity) and poorer maternal outcomes, particularly higher hysterectomy rates, compared to those with intrapartum diagnosis.
